title: Playing drums and trying every instrument
summary: He played drums and trumpet together and rented other instruments out of curiosity.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: It says in John Chilton's book that you originally played drums.

Yes, with a trumpet band; I played the trumpet and the drums. I used to take dates like that. I had a record player, it even had a straw needle on it and I played the drums with whoever was around on the record or the radio. I played the trumpet at the same time. That all went together.
That must have made you more marketable as a player.

I don't know; in those days I didn't think of it in those terms. It was curiosity. There were all sorts of instruments that I would rent from the high school, tenor saxophone, tuba; things like that. I was always fascinated by the sound of the instruments, any kind of instrument. I even tried the fiddle but that didn't
But as far as the violin goes, you learned the mechanics of the instrument.
Or the Ukelele, they're about the same thing; you knew that you had to move your fingers this way.
At least you know what works and doesn't work for a string player.
